summary: FILTER restricts which input rows contribute to a particular aggregate without removing rows needed by other aggregates in the same query.
documentation: FILTER restricts which input rows contribute to a particular aggregate without removing rows needed by other aggregates in the same query. Each aggregate can apply its own condition, enabling several related measures in one grouped pass.
returns: team, total and ready_count, ordered by team.
caution: An outer WHERE clause would also change total. NULL status does not satisfy status = ready, but its row still contributes to COUNT(*).
scenarios: Report total and ready jobs side by side for each team.
Compute several conditional counts for a dashboard row.
Compare reviewed and unreviewed import counts without losing the full denominator.
title: Count readiness without losing totals
problem: Return team, COUNT(*) AS total and COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status='ready') AS ready_count from jobs, grouped and ordered by team. Include teams with zero ready jobs.
hint: Keep the status predicate inside FILTER rather than WHERE.
goal: Use Aggregate FILTER clause or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
